A worked two-shot pair for one character across a cut with no reference image:
a walk toward a locked camera, then a held Medium Close-up. It was built over
several `/review` rounds, so each line below carries a reason. Treat it as a
starting point and judge the first generation before iterating further.

## The pair

Shot 1 — the approach (linter count: 80 words):

```
seedance_2_0 | 16:9 | 5s
Camera: Static locked-off, eye level, 63° FOV.
Subject: Woman, black chin-length bob, fringe, knee-length crimson coat.
Look: Night street, rain, rain-slicked asphalt. White shop light screen-left lights her face; cyan, violet neon bokeh. Face sharp.
Action: Starts full-figure, walks toward camera, gaze past lens, stops waist-up by 3s, stands breathing; left-right alternation, one foot grounded.
Audio: rain, footsteps. No music.
Consistent character appearance, same outfit and features throughout.
```

Shot 2 — the held beat (linter count: 74 words):

```
seedance_2_0 | 16:9 | 5s
Camera: Static locked-off, eye level, 63° FOV, Medium Close-up.
Subject: Woman, black chin-length bob, fringe, knee-length crimson coat.
Look: Night street, rain, rain-slicked asphalt. White shop light screen-left lights her face; cyan, violet neon bokeh. Face sharp.
Action: Standing still; tilts head screen-left, looks into lens, holds gaze, slow natural blinks.
Audio: rain. No music.
Consistent character appearance, same outfit and features throughout.
```

## Why it is built this way

- **Subject and Look are word for word identical in both shots.** With no
  reference image, the text is the only thing tying the two generations
  together. The closing consistency line only holds within one clip.
- **The walk, not the camera, changes the shot size.** The camera line says
  static and gives an angle and a field of view in degrees (`63° FOV`), not
  millimetres. Putting `Wide` to `Medium` in the Camera line reads as a zoom.
- **Shot 1 states the opening frame and a timing** (`Starts full-figure`,
  `stops waist-up by 3s, stands breathing`) so the model neither stretches the
  walk over all five seconds nor invents an action for the leftover time.
- **Shot 2 opens already standing still** and gives the eyes something to do
  (`holds gaze, slow natural blinks`), so the last three seconds are not a
  frozen stare.
- **Left and right are from the camera** (`screen-left`), and the light
  source is a shop light, not a "sign", which tends to render garbled lettering.
- **"wet" is avoided** (`rain-slicked asphalt`): the linter flags it as a
  provider-side false positive.

## Known trade-offs and open points

- Cut for the 80-word budget: `Red only in her coat`, `low-key`, `boots`, and the
  fuller gait wording (`heel first, strict left-right alternation`).
- Shot 1 ends `waist-up` and shot 2 is a Medium Close-up, so the cut steps in
  on purpose. A gaze side for `gaze past lens` and a head pose at the stop are
  not set.
- Both shots are static, so the cut changes only the shot size.
- Without a reference image the face may vary between generations. If you attach
  one, use a synthetic character image: the filter memory (F-004) records that
  real-person face uploads are blocked on Seedance 2.0.
- Confirm `16:9`, `5s` and the default mode live (`higgsfield model get
  seedance_2_0`) before spending credits. The specs snapshot behind the checks
  was 50 days old when this was written.
